title: Precision Pane: Per-Token Cost Lattice & Attribution Export Flow
creator: Sofia Chen
description: Build a compact, role-aware 'Precision Pane' inside Redwood Console that surfaces per-token cost breakdowns as a lattice visualization and enables robust exports. The goal is to help engineers and finance users reconcile spikes to individual prompts, attribution tags, and pricing slabs (including discounts and infra surcharge). This ticket covers design prototypes, copy, export schema, and handoff notes for engineering. Key constraints: must work within existing Console layout, support streaming rows for large datasets, and include a lightweight scenario builder to simulate pricing policy changes for a selected time range.
acceptance_criteria:
- Lattice UI prototype (desktop) in Figma with node drilldown and compact waterfall available
- Export modal with CSV/Parquet/NDJSON presets that include token-level columns (timestamp, request_id, user_id/team, model, token_type, tokens, model_cost, infra_surcharge, discounts, final_unit_cost)
- Two role presets: Finance (cost-first columns) and Engineering (latency/trace links + KV cache hit rate)
- Export includes attribution tags and preserves order for streaming consumers
- Design spec includes responsive layout rules for narrow console panes and accessibility color contrast checks
- Handoff notes list backend schema and pagination patterns for large exports
engineering_notes: Backend must expose token-level ledger endpoint with cursor-based pagination and optional filters (model, team, attribution_tag, date_range, min_tokens). CSV export should stream rows server-side to avoid memory spikes. Include columns: timestamp, request_id, route, user_id, team, model, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, total_tokens, token_type (prompt|completion|system), cache_hit (true/false), model_cost_usd, infra_surcharge_usd, discount_usd, effective_cost_usd, pricing_slab_id. Consider precomputed hourly aggregates for UI lattice to keep render time under 300ms for 30k rows. Coordinate with ENG-22890 for API schema and ENG-23001 for export infra.
review_comments:
2025-02-18 - Noah Patel (PM): Prefer 'effective_cost_usd' as last column and include human-readable slab name.
2025-02-20 - Lina Gomez (Engineer): Need agreement on token_type taxonomy (we used 'system' previously; confirm). Also request that sample export includes 10k rows for QA.
2025-02-24 - Marcus Lee (Finance reviewer): Add 'allocated_customer' column for chargeback flows; prefer percentage-based discount column as well.
2025-02-27 - Ava Martinez (Design): Adjust lattice color palette for color-blind safe palette; added notes to Figma.
decisions:
- Use a lattice visualization that groups by (team -> model -> pricing_slab) with node sizes by total_cost and inner color by avg_unit_cost.
- Default export preset = 'Finance CSV (detailed)'. Provide 'Engineering NDJSON' preset containing traces and cache flags.
- Compression: Parquet for large exports, CSV with gzip option.
- Pricing slab id included to link back to Optimize recommendations.
- Scenario builder will allow toggling a flat discount % and re-run cost projection client-side for preview only (no backend charge).
next_steps:
1) Align API schema with ENG owners (blocker: schema sign-off)
2) Finalize Figma annotations and copy for export modal
3) Produce QA export sample data (10k rows) and run perf test
4) Implement initial lattice render and export modal in a console feature branch
5) Design review on 2025-03-05 and handoff to engineering
